analysis: Two small changes examined. (1) ProviderLoop.swift lines 493-502 (head): comment update plus two new internal actor fields: addonHoldSettleTimeout (defaults to ProviderLoop.addonHoldSettleTimeoutDefault, defined in a file not supplied) and addonHoldBeforeCancellingStragglersForTesting (an internal, nil-in-production closure seam). Neither is public and neither adds an external input surface. They sit in the TB-012 add-on hold area (A-018, T-059). The settle-timeout default and the drain/cancel logic that consumes them live in ProviderLoop+AddonHold, which was not supplied, so the correctness of the release/cancellation interleaving and the bounds cannot be judged here. (2) LifecycleMailbox.swift line 81 (head): the read() open now adds O_NONBLOCK alongside O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC. This is a hardening change: opening a FIFO planted at the mailbox path without a writer no longer blocks, which removes a same-UID local DoS. The comment says non-regular files are refused afterward. The visible patch excerpt ends at the defer, so I could not confirm the fstat S_ISREG check exists after the open. If it is absent, reads on a regular file are unaffected by O_NONBLOCK, and only a FIFO/device would be read non-blockingly. O_NOFOLLOW is retained, so symlink behavior is unchanged. No change to trust boundaries, key material, attestation, or the prefix-cache threats (T-041). Remaining question for integration: confirm the regular-file check is present in LifecycleMailbox.read and that the settle-timeout consumer in AddonHold is bounded and fail-safe. No findings.
